Let \theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{8}\right). The argument \frac{15}{8} is positive, so \theta is an acute angle and can be placed in a right triangle. Call the leg adjacent to \theta x, the leg opposite it y, and the hypotenuse r. Arctangent returns opposite over adjacent, so take y=15 and x=8; then r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=\sqrt{64+225}=\sqrt{289}=17.

By the right-triangle definitions, \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}, \cos\theta=\frac{x}{r}, \tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}, \csc\theta=\frac{r}{y}, \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}, and \cot\theta=\frac{x}{y}. This expression asks for the secant of \theta, so the definition to use is \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}.

With x=8, y=15, and r=17, \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}=\frac{17}{8}.

Therefore \sec\left(\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)\right)=\boxed{\frac{17}{8}}.

With x=8, y=15, and r=17, \sec\theta=\frac{r}{x}=\frac{17}{8}.

Therefore \sec\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{17}\right)\right)=\boxed{\frac{17}{8}}.
